# `.squad/plans/integrations/00-overview.md`

```markdown
# Feature — Integrations (`integrations`)

Deliver an integrable CRM: a versioned **public API surface** with API keys and rate
limiting, an **ERP synchronisation** pipeline for customers and master data with
conflict handling, an **outbound webhook** subsystem with signing and a retryable
delivery log, and shared **messaging-provider credential** plumbing that the
`channels` story consumes. Every failure must be observable and non-fatal to ticket
handling; integration health must be visible on `/health` and in the admin UI.

Scope boundaries:

- The email / SMS / WhatsApp *adapters* belong to `channels`. This feature owns the
  credential store, secrets loading, health surface and shared HTTP/queue plumbing.
- No proprietary ERP connector — we build the generic sync engine plus a single
  reference adapter interface (`IErpCustomerSource`) so a customer-specific project
  can plug in later.
- No GraphQL.

Depends on:

- `security-admin` (`Application/Auth/Permissions.cs`, `RolePermissions.cs`) — new
  API-key scopes reuse the permission catalogue defined there.
- `customers` — ERP field mapping for `Customer` / `CustomerContact` reuses DTOs in
  `Application/Customers/Dtos/`.

## Story order

| # | File | Title | Depends on |
|---|------|-------|------------|
| 01 | `01-story-public-api-versioning.md` | Public `/api/v1` surface, DTOs, OpenAPI in all environments | — |
| 02 | `02-story-api-keys-and-rate-limiting.md` | API-key auth handler, hashed store, scopes, ASP.NET rate limiter, admin CRUD | 01, `security-admin` |
| 03 | `03-story-outbound-webhooks.md` | Webhook subscriptions, signed HMAC dispatch, retry BackgroundService, delivery log & replay | 01, 02 |
| 04 | `04-story-erp-sync-engine.md` | Generic ERP sync engine, watermark, idempotent upserts, conflict detection & queue | 01, `customers` |
| 05 | `05-story-messaging-provider-credentials.md` | Shared provider credential store, secret loading, integration health checks | 01 |
| 06 | `06-story-integrations-admin-ui.md` | Frontend: API keys, webhooks, ERP conflicts, provider credentials, health page (ar/en, RTL, 375px) | 02, 03, 04, 05 |

Cross-cutting constraints (apply to every story):

- Arabic + English, Arabic default, full RTL mirroring; every user string in both
  `frontend/src/locales/ar.json` and `frontend/src/locales/en.json`.
- Responsive down to 375px.
- Department + branch scoping via `IScopedEntity` where the entity supports it.
- New tables are `AuditableEntity` + `ISoftDeletable`; audit rows land via
  `AuditingInterceptor`.
- xUnit tests under `backend/tests/CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Tests/`;
  `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx` and
  `npm run build --prefix frontend` must pass.
- `Program.cs` `FallbackPolicy` requires authentication — new endpoints opt out only
  when they legitimately need `[AllowAnonymous]` (webhook receiver test hooks: no).
```

# `.squad/plans/integrations/01-story-public-api-versioning.md`

```markdown
# Story 01 — Public `/api/v1` surface with stable DTOs and always-on OpenAPI

## Prerequisites

- None. This is the foundation the rest of the `integrations` feature builds on.
- Read the bootstrap Swagger setup in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Program.cs`
  before editing — it already registers Swashbuckle 10 with the JWT security scheme
  (`OpenApiSecuritySchemeReference`, document-callback overload of
  `AddSecurityRequirement`). Do **not** re-register the scheme.

## Story Goal

Expose a **versioned**, **documented**, **stable** public API at `/api/v1/**` that
external systems can build against. Internal DTO renames must not break external
consumers; therefore the public surface uses its own DTOs mapped from the
`Application/*/Dtos/*` types, not the internal types directly. OpenAPI must be
served outside `Development` (currently gated by `app.Environment.IsDevelopment()`
in `Program.cs`) with a documented deprecation policy in the description.

Out of scope: authentication for the new endpoints (added in Story 02 — until then
they inherit the JWT `FallbackPolicy`).

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Program.cs` — Swagger + auth + middleware
   wiring. Note `builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen(...)`, `app.UseSwagger()`,
   `app.UseSwaggerUI()`, and the `FallbackPolicy` line. This is where you add the
   `v1` document and remove the `IsDevelopment` gate.
2. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Controllers/TicketsController.cs` — the
   canonical shape for a controller: `[Authorize]`, `[Route("api/[controller]")]`,
   ProblemDetails via thrown `Application` exceptions.
3. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Tickets/Dtos/TicketDtos.cs` and
   `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Customers/Dtos/CustomerDtos.cs` —
   source shapes to project **from** into the new `Api.Public.V1` DTOs.
4. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs` —
   confirm ProblemDetails contract; the public API must return the same shape.
5. `docs/requirements.md` area 11 for the verbatim acceptance criteria.

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — Create the public DTO namespace

Create files under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Public/V1/Dtos/`:

- `TicketV1Dto.cs` — public fields for a ticket read (id as string / GUID, reference
  number, status string, priority string, created/updated as `DateTimeOffset`, owner
  ids only, no navigation properties). Include XML doc comments — Swashbuckle picks
  them up.
- `CustomerV1Dto.cs`, `CustomerContactV1Dto.cs` — same treatment for customers.
- `PagedV1Response<T>.cs` — mirrors `Application/Common/Models/PagedResult.cs` but
  as the public shape (`items`, `page`, `pageSize`, `totalItems`, `totalPages`).
- `ErrorV1Dto.cs` — sample class only referenced by `[ProducesResponseType]` for
  Swagger; the middleware still returns RFC 7807 ProblemDetails.

**Rule:** No `Application` type is exposed on the wire from `Public.V1`. Add a
private `static class V1Mapper` per resource (`TicketV1Mapper`, `CustomerV1Mapper`)
under `Api/Public/V1/Mapping/` — plain methods, no AutoMapper.

### 2 — Add public controllers

Create files under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Public/V1/Controllers/`:

- `TicketsV1Controller.cs` with `[ApiController]`, `[Route("api/v1/tickets")]`,
  `[ApiExplorerSettings(GroupName = "v1")]`. Implement `GET` list (paged), `GET` by
  id, `POST` create, `PATCH` status change. Delegate to the existing
  `ITicketService`; project the results with `TicketV1Mapper`.
- `CustomersV1Controller.cs` — `[Route("api/v1/customers")]`, `GET` list, `GET` by
  id, `POST` create, `PUT` update. Delegate to `ICustomerService`.
- Both controllers keep `[Authorize]` for now (Story 02 adds API-key policy).

### 3 — Version + document

In `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Program.cs`:

- Replace the single `c.SwaggerDoc("v1", ...)` call with two documents:
  - `internal` — includes controllers whose `ApiExplorer` group is `null` or
    `internal`. Not for external consumption.
  - `v1` — filter to `GroupName == "v1"`. Description string must reference the
    deprecation policy: minimum 6 months notice, sunset header when deprecated,
    breaking changes only in a new major version (`/api/v2`).
- Remove the `if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())` gate around
  `app.UseSwagger()` / `app.UseSwaggerUI()` **but** keep the `internal` document
  hidden outside `Development` (filter document endpoints).
- Add `services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer()` if not already present.
- Enable XML doc generation in `CustomerSupportCRM.Api.csproj`
  (`<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>`,
  `<NoWarn>$(NoWarn);1591</NoWarn>`) and wire
  `c.IncludeXmlComments(...)` in `AddSwaggerGen`.

### 4 — Deprecation-policy static content

Create `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Public/V1/PUBLIC-API.md` with the
deprecation policy text (6-month notice, `Deprecation` and `Sunset` response
headers, changelog location). Reference this file from the `v1` Swagger
`Info.Description`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Enum stability** — internal enums (`TicketStatus`, `TicketPriority`,
  `CommunicationChannel`) may be reordered. The public mapper must emit **strings**
  (`"Open"`, `"InProgress"`) not ordinals. Enforced in `TicketV1Mapper`.
- **DateTime shape** — always `DateTimeOffset` in ISO-8601 with offset. Never
  `DateTime`.
- **Nullable navigation** — never serialise entity navigation properties; the
  mapper only picks scalar ids.
- **Public listing must respect scoping** — delegate to services that already apply
  `IScopeProvider` filtering; do not touch `IAppDbContext` directly from the public
  controller.
- **Swagger outside Dev** — verify the app does not leak the `internal` document to
  production. If unsure, document as a follow-up in a `TODO(public-api)` comment
  above the Swagger registration so the reviewer sees the risk.

## Test Plan

Add to `backend/tests/CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Tests/`:

1. `PublicApiV1MapperTests.cs` — round-trip a `Ticket` domain instance through
   `TicketV1Mapper` and assert every public field is populated and no internal-only
   field (e.g., `CreatedBy`) leaks unless intentionally public.
2. `PublicApiV1MapperTests.cs` — enum round-trip: every value of `TicketStatus` maps
   to a stable string (guard against enum reorder).
3. Manual smoke: `GET /api/v1/tickets?page=1&pageSize=5` with a valid JWT returns a
   `PagedV1Response<TicketV1Dto>`.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
3. **Swagger:** run `dotnet run --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api` and
   open `http://localhost:5178/swagger` — confirm two documents (`internal`, `v1`)
   in Dev, only `v1` outside Dev.
4. **OpenAPI export:** `curl http://localhost:5178/swagger/v1/swagger.json` returns
   a document containing `/api/v1/tickets` and `/api/v1/customers`.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `/api/v1/tickets` and `/api/v1/customers` exist and return `*V1Dto` shapes.
- [ ] No `Application/*/Dtos` type appears in a `v1` Swagger schema.
- [ ] `v1` Swagger document is served in Production; `internal` is not.
- [ ] Deprecation policy documented in `Api/Public/V1/PUBLIC-API.md` and surfaced
      in the `v1` Swagger `Info.Description`.
- [ ] XML doc comments included in the generated OpenAPI.
- [ ] Unit tests for `V1Mapper` classes pass.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to Story 02.**
```

# `.squad/plans/integrations/02-story-api-keys-and-rate-limiting.md`

```markdown
# Story 02 — API keys, scopes and per-key rate limiting

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 completed: `/api/v1/**` exists and uses public DTOs.
- `security-admin` in place: `Application/Auth/Permissions.cs` and
  `Application/Auth/RolePermissions.cs` define the permission catalogue we reuse as
  API-key scopes.

## Story Goal

External systems authenticate to `/api/v1/**` with an **API key** (or client
credentials) that is scoped to a subset of the existing permission catalogue,
completely separate from interactive user JWTs. Admins can issue, scope, rotate
and revoke keys. Keys are hashed at rest (SHA-256 + per-key salt) and shown **once**
at creation. Every public API call is rate-limited **per key** with an RFC-6585
`429 Too Many Requests` response including `Retry-After`.

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Program.cs` — `AddAuthentication`,
   `AddJwtBearer`, `AddAuthorization`, `FallbackPolicy`. You will add a second
   authentication scheme (`ApiKey`) and a per-key rate limiter policy.
2. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Auth/PermissionAuthorization.cs` — the
   permission-based authorization handler. API-key scopes flow into the same
   permission claims so `[Authorize(Policy=...)]` continues to work.
3. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Auth/Permissions.cs` — the constant
   list. New API-key scopes are strict subsets of these.
4. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContext.cs` and
   `Application/Common/Interfaces/IAppDbContext.cs` — add `DbSet<ApiKey>`.
5. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/` —
   add `ApiKeyConfiguration.cs` alongside existing ones for pattern.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Domain entity

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/ApiKey.cs`

```csharp
public class ApiKey : AuditableEntity, ISoftDeletable, IScopedEntity
{
    public string NameAr { get; set; } = "";
    public string NameEn { get; set; } = "";
    public string Prefix { get; set; } = "";          // first 8 chars, indexed, non-secret
    public string KeyHash { get; set; } = "";         // SHA-256(base64) of the full key
    public string Salt { get; set; } = "";            // per-key salt
    public string ScopesCsv { get; set; } = "";       // comma-separated Permissions.* values
    public DateTimeOffset? ExpiresAt { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? LastUsedAt { get; set; }
    public bool IsRevoked { get; set; }
    public int RateLimitPerMinute { get; set; } = 120;
    public Guid? DepartmentId { get; set; }
    public Guid? BranchId { get; set; }
}
```

### 2 — EF configuration

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/ApiKeyConfiguration.cs`

- `HasIndex(x => x.Prefix).IsUnique()`.
- `Property(x => x.KeyHash).HasMaxLength(128).IsRequired()`.
- `Property(x => x.ScopesCsv).HasMaxLength(2048)`.
- Bilingual `NameAr`/`NameEn` max 200.

Register `DbSet<ApiKey> ApiKeys { get; }` in both `IAppDbContext` and
`AppDbContext`.

**Create migration:**

```
dotnet ef migrations add ApiKeys \
  --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure \
  --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api \
  --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### 3 — Application service

**Create files** under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Integrations/`:

- `IApiKeyService.cs` with:
  - `Task<PagedResult<ApiKeyDto>> ListAsync(PagedQuery q, CancellationToken ct)`
  - `Task<ApiKeyCreatedDto> IssueAsync(IssueApiKeyRequest req, CancellationToken ct)`
    — returns the plaintext key **exactly once**.
  - `Task RevokeAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken ct)`
  - `Task<ApiKeyDto> RotateAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken ct)` — allows two live
    keys at once by issuing a new sibling and marking old with `ExpiresAt = now + 7d`.
  - `Task<ApiKeyPrincipal?> AuthenticateAsync(string presentedKey, CancellationToken ct)`
    — lookup by `Prefix`, verify hash, check `IsRevoked` and `ExpiresAt`, update
    `LastUsedAt` (fire-and-forget UPDATE, not in the request path).
- `Dtos/ApiKeyDtos.cs` (`ApiKeyDto`, `IssueApiKeyRequest` with `Scopes: string[]`
  and `RateLimitPerMinute`, `ApiKeyCreatedDto { ApiKeyDto Key, string Secret }`).
- `Validators/ApiKeyValidators.cs` — FluentValidation rules (name required,
  scopes ⊆ `Permissions.All`, `RateLimitPerMinute` between 1 and 10_000).
- `ApiKeyService.cs` — implementation. Generate 32 random bytes via
  `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32)`; format as `csk_{prefix8}_{base64url}`;
  compute `SHA256(salt || key)`; persist hash only.

### 4 — Authentication handler

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Auth/ApiKeyAuthenticationHandler.cs`

- Inherit `AuthenticationHandler<ApiKeyAuthenticationOptions>`.
- Read the key from `X-Api-Key` header (fallback to
  `Authorization: ApiKey <value>`).
- Call `IApiKeyService.AuthenticateAsync`; on success, build a `ClaimsPrincipal`
  with:
  - `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier = "apikey:{keyId}"`
  - `"permission"` claim per scope (matches the shape
    `PermissionAuthorization.cs` expects).
  - Scope-department / scope-branch claims consumed by `ScopeProvider.cs`.
- Register in `Program.cs`:

  ```csharp
  builder.Services
      .AddAuthentication()
      .AddScheme<ApiKeyAuthenticationOptions, ApiKeyAuthenticationHandler>("ApiKey", _ => { });
  ```

- Update `FallbackPolicy` to accept **either** JWT or ApiKey scheme:

  ```csharp
  var multi = new AuthorizationPolicyBuilder(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, "ApiKey")
      .RequireAuthenticatedUser().Build();
  options.FallbackPolicy = multi;
  ```

### 5 — Rate limiting

In `Program.cs`, add:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(o =>
{
    o.RejectionStatusCode = StatusCodes.Status429TooManyRequests;
    o.OnRejected = async (ctx, ct) => { /* set Retry-After, write ProblemDetails */ };
    o.AddPolicy("api-key", ctx =>
    {
        var keyId = ctx.User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value ?? "anonymous";
        var limit = int.Parse(ctx.User.FindFirst("rate-limit-per-min")?.Value ?? "120");
        return RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter(keyId, _ =>
            new FixedWindowRateLimiterOptions
            {
                PermitLimit = limit,
                Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1),
                QueueLimit = 0
            });
    });
});
app.UseRateLimiter();
```

Attach `[EnableRateLimiting("api-key")]` to the base `V1Controller` or apply
globally via `app.MapControllers().RequireRateLimiting("api-key")` filtered to
`/api/v1/**`.

### 6 — Admin CRUD controller

**Create file:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Controllers/ApiKeysController.cs`
— `[Route("api/admin/api-keys")]`, `[Authorize(Policy = Permissions.SystemAdmin)]`
(or the closest existing admin permission). Endpoints: `GET`, `POST` (returns the
plaintext key once), `POST /{id}/rotate`, `DELETE /{id}` (revoke).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Two live keys during rotation** — `RotateAsync` issues a new key and sets the
  old key's `ExpiresAt = clock.UtcNow + 7 days`. Both authenticate until expiry.
  Enforced in `ApiKeyService.RotateAsync` and `AuthenticateAsync`
  (`ExpiresAt == null || ExpiresAt > clock.UtcNow`).
- **Timing attack on hash lookup** — lookup is by non-secret `Prefix`, then a
  constant-time `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` compare of the hash.
- **Revoked key still cached** — no in-memory cache; every request hits the DB
  (indexed on `Prefix`). Rate-limit partition keys off the authenticated principal
  so revocation immediately stops the caller.
- **Key without any scope** — validator rejects (`Scopes.NotEmpty()`).
- **Rate-limit partition without a key** — falls back to `"anonymous"` partition
  with the default limit; an unauthenticated call to `/api/v1/**` is still rejected
  by the `FallbackPolicy`.
- **Scope ⊄ permissions catalogue** — validator compares against
  `typeof(Permissions).GetFields(BindingFlags.Public|Static).Select(f=>f.GetValue(null))`.

## Test Plan

Add to `backend/tests/CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Tests/`:

1. `ApiKeyServiceTests.cs`
   - `IssueAsync_ReturnsPlaintextOnceAndPersistsHash`
   - `AuthenticateAsync_AcceptsValidKey`
   - `AuthenticateAsync_RejectsRevoked`
   - `AuthenticateAsync_RejectsExpired`
   - `RotateAsync_ProducesTwoLiveKeys`
   - `AuthenticateAsync_ConstantTimeCompare` (structural — asserts use of
     `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`).
2. `ApiKeyValidatorTests.cs` — scope subset, rate-limit bounds, name required.
3. `RateLimitPartitionTests.cs` — partition key derivation from claims.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration `ApiKeys` adds one table. Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove`.
- Half-applied state (table exists, no keys issued) is safe — the auth handler
  simply finds no keys and returns `AuthenticateResult.NoResult()`, falling through
  to JWT.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
3. **Manual:** issue a key via `POST /api/admin/api-keys` with a JWT, capture the
   plaintext once, then `curl -H "X-Api-Key: <value>" http://localhost:5178/api/v1/tickets`.
4. **429 smoke:** loop the call above above the configured rate limit and confirm
   a `429` with `Retry-After` and RFC 7807 body.
5. **Regression:** existing JWT endpoints still authenticate — run any UI login
   flow against `frontend`.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `ApiKey` entity, migration and configuration in place.
- [ ] `POST /api/admin/api-keys` returns the plaintext exactly once; subsequent
      reads return only the prefix.
- [ ] `X-Api-Key` authenticates against `/api/v1/**`.
- [ ] Scope claims are enforced by the existing `PermissionAuthorization` handler.
- [ ] Per-key rate limit returns `429` with `Retry-After`.
- [ ] Rotate produces two live keys for 7 days; revoke is immediate.
- [ ] Unit tests pass.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to Story 03.**
```

# `.squad/plans/integrations/03-story-outbound-webhooks.md`

```markdown
# Story 03 — Outbound webhooks: subscriptions, HMAC signing, retry BackgroundService, delivery log

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 (public DTOs — webhook payloads reuse the `*V1Dto` types so external
  receivers see the same schema as the pull API).
- Story 02 (API-key auth — the admin webhook endpoints reuse the permission model).

## Story Goal

Notify external systems of ticket and customer events over HTTP, out of band from
the request path. Each subscription has a URL, a set of subscribed event types, and
its own HMAC secret. Deliveries are signed, retried with exponential backoff, logged
in full, and admin-replayable. **A failing subscriber must not affect ticket
handling.**

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Services/ChannelDispatchHostedService.cs` —
   canonical shape for a queue-plus-BackgroundService pattern in this repo. Copy the
   structure for `WebhookDispatchHostedService`.
2. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Channels/OutboundDispatcher.cs` —
   another dispatch example, including retry logic. Reuse ideas, don't inherit.
3. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Tickets/TicketService.cs` and
   `TicketService.Operations.cs` — the mutation methods that must **enqueue** a
   `WebhookEvent` after a successful commit. Look for the end of `CreateAsync`,
   `UpdateAsync`, `TransitionAsync`, `AssignAsync`.
4. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Customers/CustomerService.cs` — same
   for customer create/update/delete.
5. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/Notification.cs` — pattern for a
   log-like table used elsewhere.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Domain

**Create files** under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/`:

- `WebhookSubscription.cs`
  ```csharp
  public class WebhookSubscription : AuditableEntity, ISoftDeletable, IScopedEntity
  {
      public string NameAr { get; set; } = "";
      public string NameEn { get; set; } = "";
      public string TargetUrl { get; set; } = "";
      public string Secret { get; set; } = "";        // per-subscription HMAC key
      public string EventsCsv { get; set; } = "";     // e.g. "ticket.created,ticket.updated"
      public bool IsActive { get; set; } = true;
      public int MaxAttempts { get; set; } = 8;
      public Guid? DepartmentId { get; set; }
      public Guid? BranchId { get; set; }
  }
  ```
- `WebhookDelivery.cs`
  ```csharp
  public class WebhookDelivery : AuditableEntity
  {
      public Guid SubscriptionId { get; set; }
      public string EventType { get; set; } = "";
      public string PayloadJson { get; set; } = "";
      public string SignatureHeader { get; set; } = "";
      public int AttemptCount { get; set; }
      public int? LastStatusCode { get; set; }
      public string? LastError { get; set; }
      public DateTimeOffset? NextAttemptAt { get; set; }
      public DateTimeOffset? DeliveredAt { get; set; }
      public WebhookDeliveryStatus Status { get; set; }   // Pending | Delivered | Failed | DeadLetter
  }
  ```
- `Enums/WebhookDeliveryStatus.cs` — the enum above.
- `Enums/WebhookEventType.cs` — string constants (`ticket.created`,
  `ticket.updated`, `ticket.status_changed`, `ticket.assigned`,
  `customer.created`, `customer.updated`, `customer.deleted`).

### 2 — EF configuration & migration

**Create** `Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/WebhookConfigurations.cs`:

- `WebhookSubscription`: unique index on `(TargetUrl, DepartmentId, BranchId)`;
  `Secret` max 128; `TargetUrl` max 2048; `EventsCsv` max 2048.
- `WebhookDelivery`: index on `(Status, NextAttemptAt)` for the poll query;
  `PayloadJson` `nvarchar(max)`.

Register `DbSet<WebhookSubscription>` and `DbSet<WebhookDelivery>` on
`IAppDbContext` and `AppDbContext`.

Run:

```
dotnet ef migrations add Webhooks \
  --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure \
  --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api \
  --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### 3 — Application service

**Create** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Integrations/Webhooks/`:

- `IWebhookService.cs`
  - `Task<PagedResult<WebhookSubscriptionDto>> ListAsync(PagedQuery q, ...)`
  - `Task<WebhookSubscriptionDto> CreateAsync(CreateWebhookRequest req, ...)` —
    generates a per-subscription secret (32 random bytes, base64), returns it once.
  - `Task UpdateAsync(...)`, `Task DisableAsync(...)`, `Task RotateSecretAsync(...)`
  - `Task EnqueueAsync(string eventType, object payload, Guid? departmentId, Guid? branchId, CancellationToken ct)`
    — reads matching active subscriptions, inserts one `WebhookDelivery` per
    subscription with `Status = Pending`, `NextAttemptAt = clock.UtcNow`.
  - `Task<PagedResult<WebhookDeliveryDto>> ListDeliveriesAsync(WebhookDeliveryQuery q, ...)`
  - `Task ReplayAsync(Guid deliveryId, ...)` — resets `Status = Pending`,
    `AttemptCount = 0`, `NextAttemptAt = now`.
- `WebhookService.cs` — implementation, inject `IAppDbContext`, `IClock`.
- `Dtos/WebhookDtos.cs`, `Validators/WebhookValidators.cs`.

### 4 — Dispatcher BackgroundService

**Create** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Services/WebhookDispatchHostedService.cs`
(match the style of `ChannelDispatchHostedService.cs`):

- Poll every 5s (config: `Webhooks:PollInterval`).
- Take up to 50 `Pending` deliveries where `NextAttemptAt <= now`.
- For each, POST the `PayloadJson` with headers:
  - `Content-Type: application/json`
  - `X-Webhook-Event: {eventType}`
  - `X-Webhook-Delivery: {deliveryId}`
  - `X-Webhook-Timestamp: {unix seconds}`
  - `X-Webhook-Signature: sha256={hex HMAC}`
    where `HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + rawBody)`.
- Success (`2xx`): set `Status = Delivered`, `DeliveredAt = now`, `LastStatusCode`.
- Failure: increment `AttemptCount`; if `< MaxAttempts` set
  `NextAttemptAt = now + backoff(AttemptCount)` where backoff is
  `min(15min, 2^attempt seconds) + jitter(±20%)`; else `Status = DeadLetter`.
- Wrap the HTTP call in a `try/catch` — a poisoned subscriber must **never** throw
  out of the loop. Log via `ILogger<WebhookDispatchHostedService>`.
- Register in `Program.cs`: `builder.Services.AddHostedService<WebhookDispatchHostedService>();`
- Register a typed `HttpClient` (`services.AddHttpClient("webhooks", c => { c.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15); })`).

### 5 — Emit events from services

- In `TicketService.CreateAsync` (end of method, after `SaveChangesAsync`), call
  `webhookService.EnqueueAsync("ticket.created", TicketV1Mapper.Map(ticket), …)`.
- Same for `UpdateAsync`, status transitions, and assignment methods in
  `TicketService.Operations.cs`.
- Same for `CustomerService` create / update / delete methods.
- Inject `IWebhookService` into these services (constructor).
- **Non-blocking:** enqueue writes a DB row inside the same request; the actual
  POST happens in the BackgroundService.

### 6 — Admin controller

**Create** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Controllers/WebhooksController.cs`:
`[Route("api/admin/webhooks")]`. Endpoints: list subscriptions, create, update,
rotate secret, disable, list deliveries (filter by status/subscription/date),
replay delivery. Requires the admin permission used by Story 02's key admin.

### 7 — Documentation for receivers

Append to `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Public/V1/PUBLIC-API.md` a section
"Webhook verification" that documents:

1. Read raw body.
2. Read `X-Webhook-Timestamp`; reject if outside ±5 minutes of receiver clock.
3. Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body)`.
4. Compare hex to `X-Webhook-Signature` value after `sha256=` using constant-time
   compare.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Receiver down** — retries with exponential backoff up to `MaxAttempts`, then
  dead-letters. Enforced in `WebhookDispatchHostedService`.
- **Receiver slow (>15s)** — `HttpClient.Timeout = 15s` cancels; counted as a
  transient failure.
- **Enqueue during a failing outer transaction** — call `EnqueueAsync` **after**
  the parent `SaveChangesAsync` succeeds; failure to enqueue is logged, does not
  throw, and the caller succeeds (best-effort). Alternative when strong
  guarantees are needed: outbox table — document as follow-up TODO in
  `WebhookService.EnqueueAsync`.
- **Duplicate delivery** — receivers must dedupe by `X-Webhook-Delivery` id;
  documented in `PUBLIC-API.md`.
- **Payload contains secrets** — never include API keys or the subscription secret
  in the payload; use only `*V1Dto` shapes.
- **Replay of a `Delivered` row** — allowed; increments `AttemptCount` again.
- **Signature verification uncertainty on the receiver side** — provide a
  reference verifier (`docs/webhook-verify.md`) with a copy-pasteable snippet.

## Test Plan

Add to `backend/tests/CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Tests/`:

1. `WebhookServiceTests.cs`
   - `Enqueue_CreatesOneDeliveryPerActiveMatchingSubscription`
   - `Enqueue_IgnoresInactiveOrNonMatchingSubscriptions`
   - `Enqueue_ScopesByDepartmentAndBranch`
   - `Replay_ResetsCounters`
2. `WebhookSignatureTests.cs` — signature format, constant-time compare, timestamp
   included in the signed content.
3. `WebhookBackoffTests.cs` — backoff schedule caps at 15 minutes.
4. Fault-injection: a fake `HttpMessageHandler` that throws; assert delivery row
   moves to `DeadLetter` after `MaxAttempts` and the loop keeps processing others.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration `Webhooks` adds two tables. Rollback removes them; any pending
  deliveries are lost — acceptable because they are best-effort.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
3. **Manual:** point a `webhook.site` URL at the admin UI, create a ticket,
   confirm delivery within 5s, inspect delivery log for `Delivered` status and
   `2xx` code.
4. **Failure smoke:** point a subscription at a URL that returns `500`; observe
   retries and `DeadLetter` after `MaxAttempts` without impacting ticket saves.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Subscription CRUD available at `/api/admin/webhooks`.
- [ ] Every ticket create/update/status/assign and customer create/update/delete
      enqueues deliveries.
- [ ] BackgroundService signs with HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp + "." + body`.
- [ ] Retries follow exponential backoff with jitter, capped at 15 minutes.
- [ ] Delivery log queryable and replayable.
- [ ] A dead subscriber does **not** fail any ticket operation.
- [ ] Verification steps documented in `PUBLIC-API.md`.
- [ ] Tests pass.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to Story 04.**
```

# `.squad/plans/integrations/04-story-erp-sync-engine.md`

```markdown
# Story 04 — Generic ERP sync engine: adapters, watermark, idempotent upserts, conflict queue

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 (stable customer shape via `CustomerV1Dto` — the sync engine maps
  external records into the same fields).
- Coordinate with the `customers` feature owner on `Customer` /
  `CustomerContact` field mapping before starting.

## Story Goal

Import and update customers and related master data from an external ERP on a
schedule and on demand. The engine is:

- **Idempotent** — reconciles by a stable external id (`Customer.ExternalId`), never
  by name.
- **Restartable** — tracks a watermark per source, so an interrupted run resumes.
- **Conflict-aware** — when the same record was modified on both sides since the
  last sync, the change is *not* applied silently; a `SyncConflict` row is written
  for a human to resolve. The default resolution rule is documented in `PUBLIC-API.md`
  ("last write wins is **not** the default; ERP wins only for fields the CRM did not
  touch").
- **Pluggable** — one interface (`IErpCustomerSource`) with a filesystem/JSON
  reference adapter shipped in-repo; a customer-specific project provides a real
  adapter.

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Customers/CustomerService.cs` and
   `CustomerService.Extended.cs` — reuse the upsert logic; do not duplicate
   validation.
2. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/Customer.cs` — check whether
   `ExternalId` already exists. If not, add it in this story.
3. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Services/ReminderHostedService.cs` and
   `SlaEvaluatorHostedService.cs` — canonical scheduled BackgroundService pattern.
4. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Import/CustomerImportParsers.cs`
   — existing one-shot importer; the sync engine should reuse the parser
   abstractions where possible.
5. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Common/Interfaces/IAppDbContext.cs`
   for the shape of the DbContext seam.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Domain

**Modify** `Domain/Entities/Customer.cs`:

- If `ExternalId` is not already present, add:
  ```csharp
  public string? ExternalId { get; set; }
  public string? ExternalSource { get; set; }
  public DateTimeOffset? ExternalUpdatedAt { get; set; }
  public DateTimeOffset? LastSyncedAt { get; set; }
  ```
- Update `CustomerConfigurations.cs` with a unique index on
  `(ExternalSource, ExternalId)` filtered `WHERE ExternalId IS NOT NULL`.

**Create** `Domain/Entities/ErpSyncRun.cs`:

```csharp
public class ErpSyncRun : AuditableEntity
{
    public string Source { get; set; } = "";
    public DateTimeOffset StartedAt { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? CompletedAt { get; set; }
    public ErpSyncStatus Status { get; set; }   // Running | Succeeded | Failed | Cancelled
    public string? Watermark { get; set; }      // opaque change-token / high-water timestamp
    public int RecordsRead { get; set; }
    public int RecordsUpserted { get; set; }
    public int RecordsConflicted { get; set; }
    public int RecordsFailed { get; set; }
    public string? ErrorSummary { get; set; }
}
```

**Create** `Domain/Entities/SyncConflict.cs`:

```csharp
public class SyncConflict : AuditableEntity, ISoftDeletable
{
    public string EntityType { get; set; } = "Customer";
    public Guid EntityId { get; set; }
    public string ExternalSource { get; set; } = "";
    public string ExternalId { get; set; } = "";
    public string LocalJson { get; set; } = "";
    public string RemoteJson { get; set; } = "";
    public SyncConflictStatus Status { get; set; }   // Open | ResolvedLocal | ResolvedRemote | Ignored
    public Guid? ResolvedBy { get; set; }
    public DateTimeOffset? ResolvedAt { get; set; }
}
```

Enums under `Domain/Enums/ErpSyncEnums.cs`.

### 2 — EF configuration & migration

**Create** `Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/ErpSyncConfigurations.cs`
covering `ErpSyncRun`, `SyncConflict`. Add DbSets to `IAppDbContext` and
`AppDbContext`.

```
dotnet ef migrations add ErpSync \
  --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure \
  --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api \
  --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### 3 — Adapter interface

**Create** `Application/Integrations/Erp/IErpCustomerSource.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IErpCustomerSource
{
    string Source { get; }        // e.g. "SAP-B1", "Local-Json"
    IAsyncEnumerable<ErpCustomerRecord> ReadChangedAsync(
        string? watermark, CancellationToken ct);
    string ComputeWatermark(ErpCustomerRecord last);
}
```

**Create** `Application/Integrations/Erp/ErpCustomerRecord.cs` — POCO with
`ExternalId`, `NameAr`, `NameEn`, `Phone`, `Email`, `TaxNumber`, `Address`,
`ExternalUpdatedAt`.

**Create** `Infrastructure/Integrations/Erp/JsonFileErpCustomerSource.cs` — the
reference adapter that reads from a configured directory (`Erp:JsonSource:Path`),
one JSON file per record. Watermark = ISO timestamp of last read `ExternalUpdatedAt`.

Register both in `Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs`:

```csharp
services.AddScoped<IErpCustomerSource, JsonFileErpCustomerSource>();
```

### 4 — Sync engine

**Create** `Application/Integrations/Erp/ErpSyncService.cs`:

- `Task<ErpSyncRun> RunAsync(string source, CancellationToken ct)` — the entry
  point used by both the scheduler and the on-demand endpoint.
- Uses `ITransactionRunner` to wrap each batch of 100 upserts.
- For each incoming record:
  1. Look up local by `(ExternalSource, ExternalId)`.
  2. **Insert** when absent — no conflict.
  3. **Update** when present:
     - If `local.ModifiedAt <= run.LastSuccessfulRun.CompletedAt`
       → CRM has not touched the record since last sync → apply ERP values.
     - Else compare per-field: fields the CRM did not change since last sync take
       the ERP value; fields the CRM did change go to `SyncConflict` and are **not**
       overwritten. The rule is documented in `PUBLIC-API.md`.
  4. Update `LastSyncedAt`, `ExternalUpdatedAt`.
- Updates `ErpSyncRun` counters as it goes; sets `Status = Succeeded` and stores
  the new watermark at the end. On exception, sets `Status = Failed`,
  `ErrorSummary`, but never bubbles the exception past the scheduler — ticket
  handling stays up (acceptance criterion "degrades gracefully").

### 5 — Scheduler + on-demand endpoint

**Create** `Api/Services/ErpSyncHostedService.cs`:

- Reads `Erp:Schedule:IntervalMinutes` (default 60).
- Skips run when a `Running` `ErpSyncRun` already exists for the source
  (idempotent + no concurrent runs per source).

**Create** `Api/Controllers/ErpSyncController.cs`
(`[Route("api/admin/erp-sync")]`, admin permission):

- `POST /run/{source}` — triggers `RunAsync` on a `Task.Run`; returns `202
  Accepted` with the new `ErpSyncRun.Id`.
- `GET /runs` — paged list.
- `GET /conflicts` — paged list of `Open` conflicts.
- `POST /conflicts/{id}/resolve` with body
  `{ resolution: "local" | "remote" | "ignore" }` — writes the chosen values,
  updates `SyncConflict.Status`, `ResolvedBy`, `ResolvedAt`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Two ERP records with the same `ExternalId` in one batch** — engine processes
  in received order; the later record wins the write in that batch, and the
  duplicate detection is logged as a warning (not a conflict).
- **Missing `ExternalId` on ERP record** — record is skipped, `RecordsFailed++`,
  logged with source line/file path.
- **Reconcile-by-name** — explicitly forbidden. Only `ExternalId` matches.
  Enforced by never looking up by name in `ErpSyncService`.
- **Cancellation mid-batch** — `ITransactionRunner` rolls the batch back; the
  watermark is only advanced after a committed batch, so restart is safe.
- **Adapter throws mid-stream** — `ErpSyncRun.Status = Failed`, watermark not
  advanced, next run re-reads from the last committed watermark.
- **Conflict on a soft-deleted local** — treat as `Open` conflict; do not
  resurrect silently.
- **Long-running sync blocks the scheduler** — the hosted service checks for an
  in-progress run before starting; concurrent runs per source are impossible.

## Test Plan

Add to `backend/tests/CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Tests/`:

1. `ErpSyncServiceTests.cs`
   - `Run_InsertsNewCustomer_WhenExternalIdUnseen`
   - `Run_UpdatesCustomer_WhenCrmUntouchedSinceLastSync`
   - `Run_CreatesConflict_WhenBothSidesChanged`
   - `Run_IsIdempotent_OnRepeatedIdenticalBatch`
   - `Run_ResumesFromWatermark_AfterCrash`
   - `Run_ContinuesAfterAdapterException_WithoutCrashingHost`
2. `SyncConflictResolutionTests.cs` — each of `local`/`remote`/`ignore`.
3. `JsonFileErpCustomerSourceTests.cs` — read/emit/watermark round trip.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration `ErpSync` adds two tables and possibly columns on `Customer`
  (`ExternalId`, `ExternalSource`, `ExternalUpdatedAt`, `LastSyncedAt`). Adding
  nullable columns is safe on existing data.
- Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove` — data loss on `SyncConflict` /
  `ErpSyncRun` is acceptable.
- Half-applied state (columns added, no runs executed) is safe: `ExternalId` stays
  `null`, `Customer` behaves as before.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
3. **Manual:** drop JSON files into `Erp:JsonSource:Path`; call
   `POST /api/admin/erp-sync/run/Local-Json`; poll `GET /api/admin/erp-sync/runs`
   and confirm the counts.
4. **Conflict smoke:** edit a customer in the CRM, edit the source JSON, re-run;
   confirm `GET /api/admin/erp-sync/conflicts` returns the row.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `Customer` has stable `ExternalId` / `ExternalSource` and a unique filtered
      index on the pair.
- [ ] Sync engine matches on external id, never by name.
- [ ] Idempotent on repeated identical batches (no double insert, no ping-pong
      updates).
- [ ] Watermark is advanced only after a committed batch.
- [ ] Conflicts are surfaced via `GET /api/admin/erp-sync/conflicts`, not silently
      overwritten.
- [ ] Resolution rule is documented in `PUBLIC-API.md`.
- [ ] Scheduler + on-demand endpoint present.
- [ ] Adapter failure does not take the host down.
- [ ] Tests pass.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to Story 05.**
```

---

# `.squad/plans/integrations/05-story-messaging-provider-credentials.md`

```markdown
# Story 05 — Shared messaging-provider credentials and integration health

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 (public API + docs surface).
- Coordinate with `channels` — the SMTP/SMS/WhatsApp adapters consume
  `IProviderCredentialProvider` defined here. Confirm the boundary before writing
  code (this story owns the *credential store and health checks*; `channels` owns
  the *adapters*).

## Story Goal

Give the CRM a single, secret-safe place to configure credentials for outbound
email, SMS and WhatsApp providers, plus visible health for each integration on
`/health` and in the admin UI. Credentials must be loaded from configuration
providers (env vars, user-secrets, key vault), **never** committed to `appsettings*`,
**never** returned by any API endpoint.

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/Program.cs` — existing `AddHealthChecks()`
   with the `DbContext` check. Add tag-based filtering so `/health/integrations`
   is a separate probe.
2. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api/appsettings.json` and
   `appsettings.Development.example.json` — pattern for configuration bindings.
   Add a `Providers:` section to the example file only.
3. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Channels/OutboundDispatcher.cs` and
   `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Channels/LocalDropChannelAdapter.cs`
   — the adapter shape that will consume the new credential provider.
4. `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` — where
   to register the credential provider and health checks.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Options types

**Create** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure/Providers/ProviderOptions.cs`:

```csharp
public sealed class SmtpProviderOptions
{
    public string Host { get; set; } = "";
    public int Port { get; set; } = 587;
    public string Username { get; set; } = "";
    public string Password { get; set; } = "";    // never logged, never returned
    public bool UseStartTls { get; set; } = true;
    public string FromAddress { get; set; } = "";
}
public sealed class SmsProviderOptions { public string Endpoint {get;set;}=""; public string ApiKey {get;set;}=""; public string SenderId {get;set;}=""; }
public sealed class WhatsAppProviderOptions { public string Endpoint {get;set;}=""; public string ApiKey {get;set;}=""; public string PhoneNumberId {get;set;}=""; }
public sealed class ProvidersOptions
{
    public SmtpProviderOptions? Smtp { get; set; }
    public SmsProviderOptions? Sms { get; set; }
    public WhatsAppProviderOptions? WhatsApp { get; set; }
}
```

Bind in `Program.cs`:

```csharp
builder.Services.Configure<ProvidersOptions>(builder.Configuration.GetSection("Providers"));
```

### 2 — Credential provider abstraction

**Create** `Application/Integrations/Providers/IProviderCredentialProvider.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IProviderCredentialProvider
{
    SmtpProviderOptions? GetSmtp();
    SmsProviderOptions? GetSms();
    WhatsAppProviderOptions? GetWhatsApp();
}
```

**Create** `Infrastructure/Providers/OptionsCredentialProvider.cs` that returns
values from `IOptionsMonitor<ProvidersOptions>`. Register scoped in
`Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs`. `channels` adapters take this
dependency instead of reading configuration directly.

### 3 — Never return secrets

**Create** `Api/Controllers/ProvidersController.cs` (`[Route("api/admin/providers")]`,
admin permission):

- `GET` returns a **status DTO**: which providers are configured (`smtp:true`),
  the non-secret hints (`host`, `fromAddress`, `senderId`), and their last health
  status/timestamp. **No** password, `ApiKey`, or username.
- `POST /test/{provider}` — triggers a health check now and returns the result
  (still without echoing the secret back).

Enforce with a lint-time rule: add a comment in `ProvidersController.cs` — “**do
not** add fields backed by `Password` / `ApiKey`; audited by
`ProvidersControllerTests.cs`.”

### 4 — Health checks

Add to `Program.cs`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddDbContextCheck<AppDbContext>("db", tags: new[] { "ready" })
    .AddCheck<SmtpHealthCheck>("smtp", tags: new[] { "integrations" })
    .AddCheck<SmsHealthCheck>("sms", tags: new[] { "integrations" })
    .AddCheck<WhatsAppHealthCheck>("whatsapp", tags: new[] { "integrations" })
    .AddCheck<ErpSourceHealthCheck>("erp", tags: new[] { "integrations" });

app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
app.MapHealthChecks("/health/integrations", new HealthCheckOptions
{
    Predicate = r => r.Tags.Contains("integrations"),
    ResponseWriter = UIResponseWriter.WriteHealthCheckUIResponse  // JSON with per-check status
});
```

**Create** the four `IHealthCheck` classes under
`Infrastructure/Providers/HealthChecks/`:

- SMTP check: opens a TCP + `EHLO` when configured; degrades to `HealthStatus.Degraded`
  (not `Unhealthy`) when not configured — we do not want an unconfigured provider
  to fail readiness.
- SMS/WhatsApp checks: `GET` a provider-defined status endpoint from
  `ProviderCredentialProvider`, with a 5s timeout.
- ERP check: reports the last `ErpSyncRun.Status` for each configured source; `Failed`
  older than 2× the schedule interval → `Degraded`.

### 5 — Graceful degradation

- Adapters (owned by `channels`) must call `IProviderCredentialProvider`; when the
  section is `null`, they **log** and no-op instead of throwing. This story ships
  the interface + a fake provider to be used until `channels` picks it up.
- Any exception in a provider health check is caught inside the check itself and
  reported as `Unhealthy` with the exception message — never bubbled to
  `/health/integrations`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Secrets in `appsettings.json`** — forbidden. Only `appsettings.Development.example.json`
  documents the section shape with placeholders. Enforced by review + a unit test
  that asserts `appsettings.json` does not contain the `Providers` section.
- **Log leakage** — `Password` / `ApiKey` are never passed to `ILogger`. Test:
  `ProviderCredentialProviderTests.NeverLogsSecret`.
- **Endpoint leakage** — `GET /api/admin/providers` response DTO has no secret
  fields. Test: `ProvidersControllerTests.GetDoesNotReturnSecrets` inspects the
  DTO's public properties via reflection.
- **Provider misconfigured mid-run** — `IOptionsMonitor` hot-reloads on config
  change; adapters read a fresh snapshot each send.

## Test Plan

Add to `backend/tests/CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Tests/`:

1. `ProvidersControllerTests.cs`
   - `Get_ReturnsStatusOnly_WithoutSecrets` — reflect over the DTO; assert no
     field name matches `password|apikey|username|secret` (case-insensitive).
   - `Test_ReturnsHealthResult_WithoutEchoingSecret`.
2. `HealthCheckTests.cs`
   - `Smtp_ReportsDegraded_WhenNotConfigured`
   - `Sms_ReportsUnhealthy_WhenEndpointUnreachable`
3. `AppSettingsAuditTests.cs` — parses `appsettings.json`, asserts no `Providers`
   section exists (secrets discipline).

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`.
3. **Health:** `curl http://localhost:5178/health/integrations` returns per-check
   JSON with SMTP / SMS / WhatsApp / ERP entries.
4. **Secret discipline:** grep `appsettings.json` for `Password` — must return
   nothing under `Providers`.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `ProvidersOptions` bound from the `Providers:` section.
- [ ] `IProviderCredentialProvider` is the single seam for adapters.
- [ ] `GET /api/admin/providers` returns configuration status without secrets.
- [ ] `/health/integrations` exposes per-provider status.
- [ ] Unconfigured providers do **not** fail the primary `/health` probe.
- [ ] Secrets not committed anywhere in the repo.
- [ ] Tests pass.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to Story 06.**
```

# `.squad/plans/integrations/06-story-integrations-admin-ui.md`

```markdown
# Story 06 — Frontend: integrations admin UI (API keys, webhooks, ERP conflicts, providers, health)

## Prerequisites

- Story 02, 03, 04, 05 completed on the backend — all admin endpoints exist and
  return the DTOs referenced below.

## Story Goal

Give admins one place under **Admin → Integrations** to:

1. Issue / rotate / revoke API keys (plaintext shown once).
2. Manage webhook subscriptions and inspect / replay deliveries.
3. Trigger ERP sync runs, view history, resolve conflicts.
4. See provider configuration status (no secrets) and integration health.

Bilingual (ar default, RTL mirroring), responsive to 375px, all strings keyed.

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `frontend/src/router/index.ts` — where to add new routes under `/admin/...`.
2. `frontend/src/api/services.ts` — pattern for adding a typed service (`apiKeysApi`,
   `webhooksApi`, `erpSyncApi`, `providersApi`).
3. `frontend/src/api/client.ts` — shared axios instance, JWT header,
   `Accept-Language`, 401 refresh. Do not add a second client.
4. `frontend/src/types/api.ts` — mirror the new C# DTOs here (`ApiKeyDto`,
   `WebhookSubscriptionDto`, `WebhookDeliveryDto`, `ErpSyncRunDto`,
   `SyncConflictDto`, `ProviderStatusDto`, `IntegrationHealthDto`).
5. `frontend/src/views/admin/settings/SystemConfigView.vue` and
   `frontend/src/views/admin/sla/SlaAdminView.vue` — the visual + composable
   pattern for admin screens.
6. `frontend/src/components/StatusTag.vue` and `PageHeader.vue` — reuse.
7. `frontend/src/composables/useFormat.ts` — dates and numbers.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — API bindings

- Extend `frontend/src/types/api.ts` with the new DTOs / enums
  (`WebhookDeliveryStatus`, `SyncConflictStatus`, `ErpSyncStatus`).
- In `frontend/src/api/services.ts` add:
  - `apiKeysApi`: `list`, `issue`, `rotate`, `revoke`.
  - `webhooksApi`: `list`, `create`, `update`, `rotateSecret`, `disable`,
    `listDeliveries`, `replayDelivery`.
  - `erpSyncApi`: `runs`, `runNow`, `conflicts`, `resolveConflict`.

### 5 — RTL, digits, and 375px

- All layout classes use `ms-*`/`me-*`/`ps-*`/`pe-*`/`text-start` — no `ml-*` /

- Test each view in DevTools at 375px width — tables scroll horizontally with
  frozen first column, dialogs are full-height on mobile.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Plaintext key dialog dismissed accidentally** — the dialog blocks the
  backdrop, requires an explicit "I saved the key" confirm before it closes.
- **Rotate produces two keys** — UI shows both with badges "Legacy (expires in
  Xd)" and "Current".
- **Webhook delivery of very large payload** — payload cell truncates at 2 KB
  with "Show full" toggle; the network call fetches full body only on demand.
- **Concurrent conflict resolution** — server returns `409 Conflict`; UI
  refreshes the row and shows a toast.
- **Health check unreachable** — UI still renders the last known status with a
  stale timestamp; a spinner marks "checking now" when the user clicks Test.

1. **Frontend builds:** `npm run build --prefix frontend`.
2. **Frontend runs:** `npm run dev --prefix frontend` and navigate `/admin/integrations/api-keys`,
   `/webhooks`, `/erp-sync`, `/providers`.
3. **Locale toggle:** switch to Arabic; confirm `dir="rtl"` and no reversed
   numerics inside `ltr-nums` spans.
4. **Regression:** existing admin views still render.
